questions.question: A full turn measures 360°. Ravi splits a full turn into 12 equal parts, so each part is 30°. He draws an angle that covers exactly 2 of those parts. What kind of angle is it?
options: Acute, because 2 × 30° = 60°, which is less than 90°
Right, because it is made of exactly 2 equal parts
Obtuse, because 60° is bigger than 30°
Reflex, because the angle covers 2 whole parts of the turn
questions.explain: Find the size first: 2 parts × 30° = 60°, and any angle under 90° is acute. The trap is comparing the angle to one part (30°) instead of to a right angle (90°).

questions.question: A full turn measures 360°. Amara splits a full turn into 4 equal quarter-turns, so each quarter-turn is 90°. She spins her desk chair through exactly 2 of those quarter-turns. What kind of angle has she turned through?
options: Obtuse, because it is bigger than one quarter-turn
Straight, because 2 × 90° = 180°, exactly half a full turn
Reflex, because two right angles is a lot of turning
Right, because it is built out of right angles
questions.explain: Two quarter-turns make 2 × 90° = 180°, and exactly 180° has its own name: a straight angle. The trap is calling it obtuse — obtuse means between 90° and 180°, not equal to 180°.

questions.question: A full turn measures 360°. Kiera splits a full turn into 8 equal parts, so each part is 45°. She draws an angle that covers 5 of those parts, using two very short arms. What kind of angle is it?
options: Obtuse, because 225° is more than 90°
Straight, because the angle went past 180°
Reflex, because 5 × 45° = 225°, which is between 180° and 360°
Acute, because the two arms she drew are short
questions.explain: Work out 5 × 45° = 225°; anything between 180° and 360° is reflex. Two traps here: obtuse stops at 180°, and the length of the arms never changes how open an angle is.

questions.question: A full turn measures 360°. Owen splits a full turn into 24 equal parts, so each part is 15°. He draws an angle covering 6 of those parts, then makes one arm 10 cm long and the other arm only 3 cm long. What kind of angle is it?
options: Acute, because one of its arms is only 3 cm
Obtuse, because one arm is stretched out to 10 cm
Straight, because two of these angles would make 180°
Right, because 6 × 15° = 90°
questions.explain: Multiply first: 6 parts × 15° = 90°, so it is a right angle. Stretching or shortening an arm does not open or close the angle — only the amount of turn between the arms counts.

questions.question: Which of these angle measures is obtuse?
questions.explain: Obtuse means strictly between 90° and 180°, so 145° fits. The common trap is picking 210°, but once you pass 180° the angle is reflex, not obtuse.

questions.question: At the skate park in Surrey, Malik does a spin of 270°, which is three quarter-turns of 90°. What kind of angle does his spin turn through?
options: Obtuse, because 270° is more than 90°
Reflex, because 270° is between 180° and 360°
Straight, because a spin ends up facing a new way
Right, because the spin is made of quarter-turns
questions.explain: 3 × 90° = 270°, and any angle larger than 180° but smaller than 360° is reflex. The trap is thinking anything bigger than a right angle must be obtuse — obtuse stops at 180°.

questions.question: Leah's laptop screen stands straight up at 90° from the keyboard. She tips the screen back until the angle between the screen and the keyboard measures 115°. What kind of angle is it now?
options: Right, because 115° is close to 90°
Acute, because she only tipped it back a little
Obtuse, because 115° is between 90° and 180°
Reflex, because 115° is more than 90°
questions.explain: Compare 115° to the two boundaries: it is past 90° but not yet 180°, so it is obtuse. Being close to 90° is not enough — a right angle must measure exactly 90°.

questions.question: An angle is described this way: it is larger than a right angle but smaller than a straight angle. Which measure fits that description?
questions.explain: Larger than a right angle means more than 90°, and smaller than a straight angle means less than 180°, so 134° is the only fit. The trap is choosing 190°, which has already passed 180° and is reflex.

questions.question: Noah draws angle A with two arms 12 cm long, opened to 40°. He draws angle B with two arms only 3 cm long, opened to 100°. Nia says angle A must be the bigger one because its arms are much longer. Who is right, and how should the angles be named?
options: Nia is wrong: angle B is obtuse and angle A is acute, because arm length does not change how open an angle is
Nia is right: angle A is obtuse because its 12 cm arms make it large, and the bigger the arms, the wider the angle
Both angles are acute, because both fit easily on the same page, and an angle that fits so easily cannot be a big one
Nia is right: the longer 12 cm arms make angle A the bigger one, so A must be obtuse and B must be acute
questions.explain: Classify by the amount of opening only: 40° is acute and 100° is obtuse, so the short-armed angle is actually the bigger one. Long arms just mean longer lines — you could erase part of them and the angle would measure the same.

questions.question: On the classroom clock at 4:00, each hour mark is 30° apart, so the smaller angle between the hour hand and the minute hand is 120°. Going the other way around the clock face gives the rest of the full 360° turn. How should the two angles be named?
options: The smaller one is acute and the larger one is obtuse
The smaller one is obtuse and the larger one is reflex
The smaller one is obtuse and the larger one is straight
The hour hand is shorter than the minute hand, so both angles are acute
questions.explain: 4 hour marks × 30° = 120°, which is obtuse, and 360° − 120° = 240°, which is between 180° and 360°, so it is reflex. Remember the hands are just arms — a short hour hand does not make the angle smaller.

questions.question: Kai looks at two regular polygons in his math kit: a regular hexagon with sides of 2 cm, whose interior angles each measure 120°, and a square with sides of 9 cm, whose interior angles each measure 90°. Which statement about their corner angles is true?
options: The square's angles are obtuse, because its 9 cm sides are much longer, and longer sides open up a wider corner
The hexagon's angles are acute, because its 2 cm sides are short, and short sides can only hold a small corner
The hexagon's angles are obtuse and the square's angles are right, even though the square's sides are longer
Both shapes have right angles, because both are regular polygons, and regular means every corner is a square corner
questions.explain: Name each angle from its measure: 120° is between 90° and 180° so it is obtuse, and exactly 90° is a right angle. Longer sides do not make bigger corner angles — side length and angle size are two different measurements.

questions.question: Jayden unfolds a camp chair for a trip to Cultus Lake. Measured on the inside, the angle between the seat and the back rest is 100°. He then measures around the outside instead, going the long way around the same point so the two angles together make a full 360° turn. What is the outside angle, and what kind of angle is it?
options: 80°, an acute angle
260°, an obtuse angle, because 260° is much bigger than 90°
100°, an obtuse angle, because measuring the other way cannot change it
260°, a reflex angle
questions.explain: Angles around a point add to 360°, so 360° − 100° = 260°, which lands between 180° and 360° and is therefore reflex. Two traps: subtracting from 180° instead of 360°, and calling anything past 180° obtuse.
